I am a Data Analyst working in an energy company, with a PhD in Political Science and years of experience in collecting and analysing data (texts, surveys, census). This web-site is a summary of my academic work, which focused on how law and judicial institutions function in authoritarian regimes, with empirical focus on Russia. More specifically, I studied the decision-making of constitutional courts and individual strategies of judges under authoritarianism, how modern autocrats use and misuse international law, and ethnic bias in the lower level judiciary. 

In 2022-2025 I led a three-year research project *The Power and the Limits of International Law,* funded by the Federal Ministry of Education and Research (BMBF) and the Free and Hanseatic City of Hamburg under the Excellence Strategy of the Federal Government and the Länder (2022-2025). In 2021-2022 I have been a postdoctoral researcher at the Center for Russia, East Europe, and Central Asia (CREECA) at the University of Wisconsin-Madison. I hold a Ph.D. in Political Science from the Bremen International Graduate School of Social Sciences (2022), and prior to this studied Law and Sociology at Higher School of Economics, Moscow.
